# radref

> Source-checked summaries of radiology classification systems, reference measurements and
> guideline recommendations, for AI reporting assistants. Summaries only; no full texts.

## How to use

- Read `index.json` first: one line per entry with id, title, scope, status and source ids.
- Open `entries/<area>/<id>.md` for the theory: scope, definitions, criteria, management,
  pitfalls and "What the source does not say".
- To cite in a report, take the Vancouver string from `references/references.json`, by id,
  **exactly as written**. Only cite references with `"vancouver_reviewed": true`.
- Use only entries with `status: verified` to support a categorization or recommendation.
  `draft` entries are background reading only.
- If the case is outside an entry's scope, say so; do not apply the criteria.
- If the needed fact is in "What the source does not say", do not attribute it to the source.
- The physician's dictation always prevails over this base.

## Files

- [index.json](index.json): list of entries
- [references/references.json](references/references.json): all sources with checked metadata
- [docs/for-tools.md](docs/for-tools.md): full contract for consuming tools
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): how entries are written and verified
